refnamediv.refpurpose: Generic interface for acquiring named resources from local services

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: io.systemd.ResourceProvider is a Varlink interface implemented by systemd1-related components. It can be introspected and called with varlinkctl1.

A generic protocol for fetching named resources from a local service, addressed by URLs of the form provider:[PATH]/RESOURCE. systemd's pull implementation accepts such URLs wherever it accepts HTTP URLs, for example in systemd-sysupdate8 transfer definitions, which is what lets a provider ship the actual payload instead of pointing at a remote server. AcquireResource() must be called with the upgrade flag; the provider replies, optionally announcing size, and then writes the raw resource contents over the connection. An unknown name is reported as NoSuchResource, and a connection closed before the announced size was reached indicates a truncated transfer, since errors can only be reported before the upgrade.

refsect1.title: Security
refsect1.para: The protocol performs no authentication of its own: whoever may connect to the socket named in the URL may fetch the resources it serves, so access control is the socket's ownership and mode. The pull implementation connects as the user it runs as, which for system contexts is the superuser.

refsect1.title: Interface Definition
refsect1.para: The following interface definition is exposed:
refsect1.programlisting:
# Generic interface for acquiring the contents of named resources from a local service. It is addressed via URLs of the form 'provider:[/path/to/socket]/resource', which systemd-pull(1) accepts wherever it accepts HTTP URLs, e.g. in systemd-sysupdate(8) transfer definitions. The resource contents are transferred via a protocol upgrade: after the reply to AcquireResource() the connection carries the raw resource data until the provider closes it. interface io.systemd.ResourceProvider
# Acquires the resource with the specified name. Must be called with the 'upgrade' flag set. On success the provider replies (optionally announcing the size) and then writes the raw resource contents to the connection, closing it once all data has been written. Errors can only be reported before the upgrade; a connection closed before the announced size was reached indicates a truncated transfer. # [Requires 'upgrade' flag] method AcquireResource( # The name of the resource to acquire. This is the part of a 'provider:[…]/…' URL following the closing bracket and slash, i.e. an opaque, non-empty string that may contain slashes, but no '.' or '..' components. name: string ) -> ( # The size of the resource in bytes, if known. Clients may use this for progress reporting and to detect truncated transfers. size: ?int )
# No resource by the specified name exists. error NoSuchResource()

refsect1.title: Examples
refsect1.para: varlinkctl introspect SERVICE io.systemd.ResourceProvider shows the interface definition as served by SERVICE, and varlinkctl call SERVICE io.systemd.ResourceProvider.AcquireResource \ '{"name": "pool/example.raw"}' invokes its AcquireResource() method.

refsect1.title: History
refsect1.para: The io.systemd.ResourceProvider interface was added in version 263.
AcquireResource(), and NoSuchResource were added in version 263.
